cards.explanation: The answer is the Wilderness of Paran. The text says Israel traveled "…from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran." (Numbers 10:12) That's a whole string of stops before the cloud finally stays put. I've been moved around a lot in my life, and I still wouldn't know when to unpack.

The answer is False. The text says they set out "…according to the LORD’s command through Moses." (Numbers 10:13) So the tribe leaders didn't decide it. The LORD gave the command, and Israel followed.

The reason Moses gives is that the LORD has promised good things to Israel. He says, "…for the LORD has promised good things to Israel." (Numbers 10:29) He's inviting Hobab to a promise, not just a trip. And he says they'll treat Hobab well.

Hobab says he's going back to his own land and his own people. His words are, "I will not go… Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people." (Numbers 10:30) That's a clear answer. I think he's got home on his mind.

Moses says Hobab knows where they should camp in the wilderness. He says Hobab knows "…where we should camp in the wilderness…" and that he can "…serve as our eyes." (Numbers 10:31) Moses is asking Hobab to be Israel's eyes out there. It's a real need he's pointing to.

The word is "share." Moses says, "…we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us." (Numbers 10:32) He doesn't offer Hobab a wage or a trade deal. He offers a share in whatever the LORD gives.

The ark of the covenant is what travels ahead, friends. The text says "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" was "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) The ark goes out in front, and Israel sets out from the mountain of the LORD behind it. Three days of that.
The word is "resting." The ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) After three days of walking, a resting place sounds mighty good. The ark is out there looking for one.

The answer is True. The text says, "…the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp." (Numbers 10:34) So the ark goes ahead, and the cloud is overhead. Israel isn't setting out without either one.

Moses asks the LORD to rise up and scatter His enemies. He says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) He says it every time the ark sets out. It's a prayer, spoken out loud.
